newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 to 4.00 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 to 4.00 lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 3.00 to 4.00 cents per lb lower on Tuesday, on the heels of steep losses in London overnight, traders said.

London robusta futures fell sharply early Tuesday, as heavy fund selling drove prices to their lowest levels since late April. At the midday break, benchmark September was down $97 at $1,638, after ranging from $1,720 to $1,635.

Monday, New York arabica futures ending mostly lower in thin trading, with September falling 2.10 cents, to 162.00 cents, after ranging between 166.00 and 161.00 cents. Spot July, which expires in a week, rose 1.00 cent, to 187.00 cents, while the outer months closed down 0.25 to 2.65 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 25.00 cents compared with 21.90 cents at the close on Friday, while the September/December switch narrowed to 12.50 cents from 13.10 cents.

CSCE reported after Monday's close that certified coffee inventories rose for the seventh day in a row, increasing by 1,644 60-kg bags as of July 11, to 72,245 bags. An additional 19,324 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
CSCE also reported that out of 2,822 bags graded only 774 bags passed exchange approval.

Also after Monday's close, the CSCE said it will decrease margins on the July "C" coffee contract to $7,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, and on the September "C" contract to $6,000, including a $2,000 spot charge, effective July 15.
The margin on all other coffee contracts will be decreased by $2,000, to $4,000, the exchange said.

Technically, traders said the September contract may run into some chart support at 160.00 cents, but added they were now taking a closer look at the 158.00 and 155.00 levels. On the upside, they said September faced resistance at 165.00-165.50, with the next level seen near 168.00.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday that there is no damaging cold weather expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt, with temperatures averaging near to above normal through Monday.

Traders await the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report due this afternoon at 1500 EDT. They expected inventories to be little changed in June, with most preliminary estimates coming in at plus or minus 100,000 bags.
In May, GCA reported stocks of green coffee in U.S. warehouses rose by 122,000 bags, to 1,977,000 bags. Stocks in June 1996 fell by 110,000 bags, to 2,161,000 bags.
